name: Blood pressure
intro: Where the BP diary is honest and the doctor report is one tap away, and where it claims to measure blood pressure with a finger on the camera.

apps.title: BP diary (self-monitoring)
apps.verdict: BP diary honestly does one thing: it lets you quickly log blood pressure and pulse and show it to a doctor, with no ads or tricks. People praise the clean interface and easy entry but hit a 30-day ceiling on reports and no sync across devices. For a manual diary it's one of the best options in the niche.
apps.loved: Clean and pleasant interface, easy entry, PDF export for the doctor, no ads, free
apps.weak: Reports and charts only cover the last 30 days, no sync between iPhone and iPad, can't track multiple people, few notes per reading, can't bulk-delete entries
apps.whoFor: People who measure their pressure with a cuff themselves and want to keep tidy records to show a doctor.

quotes.text: Another great additional would be to type in your measurements instead of the slider.
I could not edit a date after posting had to switch to another app, lost all entered data
I’ve got 3 weeks of bps on a paper log how do I add them to this? It appears you only have this app set to “today”
reports and graphs can only be generated for the past 30 days. Developers: please add the ability to generate longer reports with all data

You do not have the ability to add any notes such as which extremity was used, what position you were in ( sitting, standing, lying), or other relevant information that could add context to the BP value
I would like to track both my mother and myself. There is no way to track multiple users. THIS IS USELESS.

apps.title: iBP Blood Pressure
apps.verdict: This is a manual-entry blood pressure diary, not a meter, and people have kept it for 10-16 years, loving the graphs and Apple Health sync. The main pain lately: data export and Withings import broke and support does not reply. Some versions crash on newer iPhones.
apps.loved: Excellent graphs and trends, Apple Health sync, simple entry, stable for years, doctors value the history
apps.weak: Broken export and email sending, dead Withings import, crashes on newer iPhones, silent support, no cross-device sync
apps.whoFor: People who measure with a real device and want a detailed long-term diary with graphs

quotes.text: The syncing to and from Apple Health remains flawless and the graphs with trended data are excellent to this day.

apps.title: Blood Pressure Companion Pro
apps.verdict: The paid version of a long-standing BP diary with strong PDF reports valued by doctors and long-term users. Its reputation is hurt by a switch to a pricey subscription that removed previously bought features and by cases of losing years of data. Export and printing sometimes break and support does not answer.
apps.loved: Easy entry and history, detailed PDF reports for the doctor, notes field, years of use
apps.weak: Switch to pricey subscription stripped paid features, loss of years of data, broken export and printing, silent support, tiny font for seniors
apps.whoFor: People who have logged BP for years, value detailed doctor reports, will pay a subscription and keep a data backup.

quotes.text: My doctors have recommended it to others patients after they saw the reports and history the app provided by me simply recording my bp into the app.
when trying to pull the reports for my doctor visit this afternoon there is not a print option.

apps.title: Blood Pressure Log Feeltracker
apps.verdict: A solid blood-pressure log where you can record a reading even by photographing the monitor screen, with date, time and a note, and doctors value it. Its weak spots are the paid AI summary, a questionable tie to the Omron brand and cases of data loss after updates. Overall it does its job conveniently and more reliably than most rivals.
apps.loved: Record a photo of the monitor screen with date and note, convenient for the doctor, simple and reliable, stores and shares history
apps.weak: Useful features moved behind a paywall, records lost after updates, expensive pro version, not the official Omron app despite expectations, occasionally closes on entry
apps.whoFor: For those who log pressure by hand and want an easy way to capture readings and share history with a doctor

apps.title: BreathNow - blood pressure app
apps.verdict: This is not a pressure meter but breathing exercises and meditations that help you relax and genuinely bring pressure and stress down. Users note a quick if short effect and handy data export. The weak spot is camera pulse measurement: readings jump from 42 to 186.
apps.loved: Breathing exercises, meditations with a pleasant voice, real drop in pressure and stress, data export, not pushy
apps.weak: Camera pulse readings lie and jump around, session cut from 3 minutes to 1, sometimes fails to save results
apps.whoFor: People who want to calm down and gently lower pressure through breathing, not measure it precisely

apps.title: Blood Pressure Companion
apps.verdict: A years-proven manual BP diary that doctors and cardiac rehab recommend to patients for its simple logging and reports. Lately intrusive ads that cover the entry buttons and cases of data loss are killing it. It used to be a great free tool but is now hard to use.
apps.loved: Simple entry and history, clear reports for the doctor, years of stable use, recommended by cardiologists
apps.weak: Intrusive ads cover buttons, loud audio ads, cases of losing all data, no Health sync, no editing entries
apps.whoFor: People who want a simple free BP journal with doctor reports and can tolerate aggressive ads.

quotes.text: This is OK to keep a record of your blood pressure but I don’t like that you’re not able to just type in your systolic and diastolic and you’re forced to use the dial.
When we hit the senior level, we can relax about having a 120/80 bp reading. Many GOOD practitioners recommend it in the 130-140/80-90.
the notes are hidden. In order to see your notes (ie. L Arm, after walk) that you made

apps.title: Blood Pressure Monitor
apps.verdict: This is a manual-entry diary for three pressure numbers, not a meter, and people have kept it for over a decade, valuing the simplicity and emailing history to their doctor. The recent trouble is that ads went full-screen and pop up right while you enter data, sometimes in the doctor's office. Export also broke and there is no Apple Health sync.
apps.loved: Simple entry and setup, emailing history to the doctor, reliability and data since 2013, handy graphs
apps.weak: Aggressive full-screen ads over data entry, broken data export, no Apple Health sync, sometimes freezes on opening
apps.whoFor: People who measure with a real device and want a simple long-term diary, if they can tolerate the ads

quotes.text: when I’m having an issue, I am able to open this app to look back on all my previously stored readings. Very helpful and reliable.

apps.title: iHealth MyVitals
apps.verdict: A companion for iHealth cuffs, valued for its color coded pressure zones and clear trends. Weak spots are the flaky Apple Health sync where heart rate goes through but blood pressure doesn't, plus a forced voice AI assistant you can't turn off.
apps.loved: Color coded pressure zones, clear trends and history, easy cuff pairing, accuracy
apps.weak: Blood pressure doesn't always sync to Apple Health, network timeouts on login and upload, forced AI assistant with no off switch, inconsistent repeat readings
apps.whoFor: Owners of iHealth cuffs who want clear trends and color indication

quotes.text: Currently the app only supports sending over heart rate to HealthKit from the blood pressure monitor. It would be nice if the developer would enabled syncing of blood pressure to HealthKit
twice now have had the issue where the app doesn’t recognize the device (Relion Platinum Blood Pressure Cuff)
The app keeps track of trends and alerts the user when their blood pressure is high by changing colors. Green is good yellow is borderline and orange is extremely high blood pressure.

apps.title: Health Diary by MedM
apps.verdict: A serious health diary that syncs with real Bluetooth cuffs and oximeters and helps gather data for a doctor. It is held back by flaky Apple Health sync and a paywall on what many see as a basic feature. Bluetooth drops on some devices.
apps.loved: Pairing with real Bluetooth cuffs, many metrics, printing and reports for the doctor, years of stable use
apps.weak: Apple Health sync locked behind payment, unstable Bluetooth, premium pressure, iPad orientation issues, tiny font
apps.whoFor: Owners of Bluetooth cuffs and oximeters who want one diary of metrics for their doctor and do not mind paying for sync.

quotes.text: If there are two users, the report is only for one user and you don’t know which one. Confusing.

apps.title: Hello Heart • For heart health
apps.verdict: Hello Heart is handed out by insurers along with a cuff, and it earns praise for pressure tracking with trends and tips. But it loses Bluetooth connection to the cuff, sometimes wipes years of data, and its motivational messages confuse a rise with a drop in pressure.
apps.loved: Clear trends and tips, easy to show a doctor, reminders keep you on track, comes free through insurance
apps.weak: Loses Bluetooth link to the cuff, years of data vanish, Apple Health sync fails, access dies when the insurance program ends, confused motivational messages
apps.whoFor: People given the cuff and app by an insurer or employer to monitor blood pressure

quotes.text: The trend charts show your progress and helpful hints and reminders help keep you on track. They say “what gets measured gets done” and this tool definitely helps you stay focused
My pressure was 128/84 then 126/80 the next day and it gave me a message that says "your pressure went up let's see what we can do to get it down"

apps.title: Blood Pressure App Monitor
apps.verdict: A simple free BP log with no ads and no subscription push, which users appreciate. The main gripe is that the 'elevated' thresholds are too strict and alarm people at numbers normal for them. It lacks trend charts, entry editing and age adjustment.
apps.loved: Simple entry, no ads, no subscription selling, pulse and averages, free
apps.weak: Overly strict elevated thresholds, no trend graphs, cannot edit an entry, ignores age, weak export feature
apps.whoFor: People who want a simple free ad-free BP log, understand their own normal ranges and do not rely on the app's assessment.

quotes.text: This app is easy to use. Just measure and record. No extras
I’ve had some good readings and the app still says it’s “stage 1” that even a nurse says is not true.

apps.title: Blood Pressure App ++
apps.verdict: A plain manual blood pressure log with a clean design and readable charts you can show your doctor. The aggressive subscription push on every launch and the confusing cancellation flow spoil it. Users complain they cannot edit entries or backdate readings.
apps.loved: Easy entry, clear charts, simple to share with a doctor, pleasant interface
apps.weak: Pushy premium prompts, hard to unsubscribe, no editing or deleting entries, no backdating, history capped at 7 days
apps.whoFor: People who want a simple BP journal with clear charts for doctor visits and can tolerate constant upsell.

quotes.text: I would like to go back and add a note and it won’t let me do that. Also I sometimes take three readings in a row and it would be nice to delete one or two of them.
Although I like this App, I need a way to edit my mistakes. Some of us are using these Apps per Dr. order to keep track of our Blood Pressure
why it declares blood pressure of 114/81 as “low BP”, which is a far cry from the <90/<60 that every medical org
Views are limited to 7 days, which is not very helpful to long term compare and analysis.

apps.title: Blood Pressure Tracker SmartBP
apps.verdict: SmartBP is a manual blood pressure diary with charts, medication reminders and Apple Health sync, which people praise. What annoys them is the aggressive subscription push on every tap and ads that falsely imply the app measures pressure itself.
apps.loved: Easy entry and blood pressure charts, medication reminders, Apple Health integration, helps track trends
apps.weak: Aggressive purchase screens at every step, ads misleadingly imply it measures pressure, pricey subscription, buggy sync and Bluetooth cuff pairing
apps.whoFor: People who measure pressure with their own cuff and want a tidy diary with reminders

apps.title: A&D Heart Track
apps.verdict: The official companion app for A&D blood-pressure monitors that works with the cuff and stores history for the doctor. Its strength is real readings and export, its weakness is flaky Bluetooth pairing and frequent crashes during measurement. Many are annoyed by the mandatory account login and that data goes through the company's service rather than straight into Apple Health.
apps.loved: Works with a real cuff, stores and exports history, easy to show the doctor, simple to use
apps.weak: Bluetooth pairing drops, crashes during measurement, mandatory account login, worse Apple Health integration than the old app, short history and notes not saved
apps.whoFor: For owners of A&D monitors who need reading sync and history for the doctor

quotes.text: Apparently, you are supposed to click on + Measurement and not Start. When I do that, it works just fine.
Only saves 30 days history.
comments saved to individual blood pressure readings are not retained.

apps.title: Withings
apps.verdict: The Withings ecosystem with a cuff and scale, valued for the depth of its health data and Apple Health integration. But updates keep breaking sync, the app mixes up family members' data, crashes on launch, and part of the features sit behind a 99 dollar a year subscription.
apps.loved: Lots of health data, convenient hardware and app pairing, Apple Health integration when it works
apps.weak: Sync keeps breaking after updates, launch crashes, mixes up data from different users, pricey subscription, no way to reach support
apps.whoFor: Owners of Withings hardware willing to tolerate glitches for one unified health ecosystem

quotes.text: Most recent update seems to destroy automatically pushing data to Apple health. Now, unlike before, the Withings app has to be manually opened and refreshed
I Shared my Whithings BPM connect device with my wife, followed all the instructions and now my data is mixed with hers.

apps.title: OMRON connect US/CAN/EMEA
apps.verdict: The official OMRON app that for years was simple and handy for daily blood pressure checks. A recent redesign broke it all, history is buried deep, it demands a login every launch, and Excel export and Apple Health sync work only half the time.
apps.loved: OMRON cuff accuracy, reliable hardware and app pairing, used to be simple and convenient, responsive support
apps.weak: New redesign buried the reading history, demands login every launch, Excel export barely works, blood pressure doesn't sync to Apple Health, tiny font
apps.whoFor: Owners of OMRON cuffs willing to put up with the awkward new interface

quotes.text: This app, although efficient at monitoring and recording BP on the machine and in this app is HORRIBLE at emailing results in Excel format. I need the data in excel format to share with my doctor.
I get heart rate data in Apple Health, but no blood pressure readings.

apps.title: Equate Heart Chart
apps.verdict: The app for Walmart's Equate cuffs, valued for simple blood pressure logging, charts and per reading notes with no paywalls. It's let down by unstable Bluetooth to the cuff, registration failures with a network error, and no Apple Health sync.
apps.loved: Simple blood pressure logging, charts and trends, notes on each reading, no subscription or paywalls
apps.weak: Bluetooth to the cuff often won't connect, registration fails with a network error, no Apple Health sync, readings sometimes vanish from history, white screen
apps.whoFor: Owners of Walmart's Equate cuffs who want a free simple blood pressure diary

quotes.text: Blue tooth never connects
Device no longer connects to the phone via Bluetooth. I have to enter everything manually!
easy to change user, goes on with the start button

apps.title: Blood Pressure Tracker •
apps.verdict: A simple manual blood pressure diary praised for easy doctor reports and a clear interface. It breaks after iOS updates, crashes on Apple Health sync and loses all data on reinstall, plus it locks access to your own records without a subscription.
apps.loved: Easy doctor reports, clean clear interface, printable history, a working free version exists
apps.weak: Crashes after iOS updates, loses all data on reinstall, Apple Health sync fails, duplicate entries from Apple Health, locks data access without subscription
apps.whoFor: People who measure pressure with their own cuff and want a simple diary with doctor reports

apps.title: Blood pressure app+
apps.verdict: A manual BP journal with cute posture icons, but a paywall to enter and ads that bother even paying users. Its pressure classification does not match medical norms and confuses people. Many expected the app to measure BP itself and were let down.
apps.loved: Simple data entry, cute posture icons, handy during pregnancy
apps.weak: No trying before subscribing, pricey 70-90 dollar plans, ads on every launch, inaccurate pressure classification, no Apple Health sync, no editing entries
apps.whoFor: People after a very simple manual log who will pay a subscription and do not expect auto-measurement.

quotes.text: I would like to go back and add a note and it won’t let me do that. Also I sometimes take three readings in a row and it would be nice to delete one or two of them.
Although I like this App, I need a way to edit my mistakes. Some of us are using these Apps per Dr. order to keep track of our Blood Pressure
why it declares blood pressure of 114/81 as “low BP”, which is a far cry from the <90/<60 that every medical org
Views are limited to 7 days, which is not very helpful to long term compare and analysis.

apps.title: My Blood Pressure Journal
apps.verdict: An honest manual blood-pressure log with pulse and notes that does exactly what it promises. The main problem is aggressive ads: after every entry a full-screen banner pops up, sometimes unclosable without restarting the app. There are also data losses and small date bugs.
apps.loved: Easy entry of pressure and pulse, notes on each entry, simple and clear, easy to show the doctor
apps.weak: Full-screen ad after every entry, ads keep showing even after paying, data gets lost, date and time drift, numbers cut off on screen
apps.whoFor: For those who want a simple pressure diary and can tolerate intrusive ads in exchange for being free

quotes.text: Used to be really good! But on latest version, I can no longer share my statistics with my doctor. I am disappointed.
you can add notes when you take your blood pressure.

apps.title: HealthBit-Lifestyle&Heart Care
apps.verdict: HealthBit is pitched as heart care with camera-based blood pressure, but really only the pulse works reliably while pressure drifts nearly 40 points from a cuff. The ads promise more than is there, and some features unlock only after paying for Pro, which doesn't always help. As a manual tracker it's acceptable, as a pressure meter it isn't.
apps.loved: Simple for seniors, the idea of gathering readings together, pulse measurement
apps.weak: Camera blood pressure is inaccurate, off from a cuff by up to 39 points, ads promise more than exists, some features Pro-only, measurement sometimes won't start, charges and hard cancellation
apps.whoFor: Seniors and people who want a simple pulse tracker and are fine entering blood pressure by hand.

apps.title: Instant Pulse - Blood Pressure
apps.verdict: Instant Pulse measures pulse and stress by camera and promises signs of atrial fibrillation, but people with real episodes report it shows a regular rhythm in the middle of an attack. Instructions confuse which camera to use, and stress and oximetry come with no explanation. Add a yearly charge with no trial, which leaves many feeling locked in.
apps.loved: Quick pulse reading, some find the results accurate, helps keep an eye on the heart
apps.weak: Afib signs are unreliable, shows normal during an episode, confusing camera instructions, no explanation for stress and oxygen, yearly charge with no trial, ad at the bottom
apps.whoFor: People who want a quick pulse on their phone and don't rely on the app for atrial fibrillation.

apps.title: Hearty : Heart Rate,Stress, BP
apps.verdict: Hearty gathers data from your devices and used to be liked, but the AI update wiped out previously paid features and moved everything to subscription. People complain about a lost stress monitor, broken history screens, and that the app doesn't measure blood pressure at all. The potential shows, but the current state let many down.
apps.loved: Gathers data from all devices in one place, tracks pulse and steps, lots of health info
apps.weak: AI update removed previously purchased features, everything moved to subscription, stress monitor gone, errors on history screens, doesn't measure blood pressure, AI analysis doesn't work
apps.whoFor: Apple Watch owners who want a readings aggregator, not phone-based blood pressure measurement.

apps.title: Wellmy - Heart Rate Monitor
apps.verdict: The app asks you to place a finger on the camera and promises blood pressure, but people compare it to a home cuff and see tens of points of drift. On top of that comes a pushy subscription instead of the promised free access and charges after the trial. As a log of readings it is fine, as a measuring tool it earns no trust.
apps.loved: Simple interface, quick pulse reading, occasional health check-in questions
apps.weak: Blood pressure is inaccurate, off from a cuff by 30-50 points, hidden paid subscription instead of being free, charges after the trial, hard to cancel
apps.whoFor: People who want a quick pulse on their phone and are willing to enter blood pressure by hand rather than trust the camera.

apps.title: Finger Blood Pressure: BP Mate
apps.verdict: It measures pressure with a finger on the camera and demands calibration, after which it simply echoes the numbers you entered, and gives random ones without it. Pulse often shoots to 150-180 when it is really 70. Add a paywall after about a dozen readings and complaints about charges with no refund.
apps.loved: Easy to carry, simple interface, numbers look plausible after calibration
apps.weak: Random numbers without calibration and mere echoes of your data with it, pulse far off, paywall after a few readings, refund trouble
apps.whoFor: At most a rough estimate, but you cannot rely on it for real blood pressure control

apps.title: Blood Pressure App
apps.verdict: It used to be a simple free log doctors liked for its printouts, but an update locked features behind a paywall and added ads. Many lost their history after the update or a phone change because there is no export or sync. There is no camera measurement here, it is manual entry.
apps.loved: Handy printouts for the doctor, quick entry, simple interface in the old version
apps.weak: Features moved behind a paywall, ads after the update, lost history on update and phone change, no export or HealthKit sync, interface became cluttered
apps.whoFor: For those who valued the old simple version it is now questionable, still usable for doctor printouts, but data is easily lost

quotes.text: I would like to go back and add a note and it won’t let me do that. Also I sometimes take three readings in a row and it would be nice to delete one or two of them.
Although I like this App, I need a way to edit my mistakes. Some of us are using these Apps per Dr. order to keep track of our Blood Pressure
why it declares blood pressure of 114/81 as “low BP”, which is a far cry from the <90/<60 that every medical org
Views are limited to 7 days, which is not very helpful to long term compare and analysis.

apps.title: Heartica: Heart Rate Monitor
apps.verdict: Heartica claims to read blood pressure and even blood sugar through the phone camera, but people report only the pulse actually works and the rest has to be typed in by hand. Many are met by a purchase screen that won't close and charges despite the promise not to bill. The pulse is handy for some, but most of the advertised features aren't really there.
apps.loved: Quick pulse reading, front-camera mode, propping the phone on a table frees your hands
apps.weak: Blood pressure and sugar aren't read by the camera, purchase screen won't close, billed despite a promised free trial, hard to cancel, confusing heart-age numbers
apps.whoFor: People who just want a quick pulse check and don't expect real blood pressure or sugar from the camera.

apps.title: Heart Rate: Pulse Monitor & BP
apps.verdict: It used to promise camera pressure measurement, but an update removed that feature and now you must enter pressure by hand, which angers those who bought it for exactly that. Pulse also drifts to dangerous sub-40 values, causing one user real stress and extra medical tests. Plus trouble cancelling the subscription.
apps.loved: Fast pulse reading, simple interface, instant feedback
apps.weak: Pressure measurement removed, pulse lies to dangerous levels, false free promise, hard to cancel and get a refund
apps.whoFor: At most a quick glance at pulse, not fit for blood pressure

apps.title: Blood Pressure App-BP Tracker
apps.verdict: Blood Pressure App-BP Tracker hints in ads at measuring blood pressure with the phone, but in reality everything except the pulse is entered by hand. Many feel misled and complain about charges for something that duplicates the Apple Watch. As a manual diary with a couple of readings it works, but it doesn't do the main advertised thing.
apps.loved: Simple entry, gathers pulse and oxygen in one place, easy to start
apps.weak: Doesn't measure blood pressure, everything but pulse is manual, misleading ads, charges and hard cancellation, duplicates Apple Watch features, ads
apps.whoFor: People willing to enter blood pressure by hand who want a simple readings log, not phone measurement.

apps.title: Health Partner: Pulse & Sugar
apps.verdict: Health Partner advertises camera-based blood pressure and sugar, but reviews call it a plain manual log with misleading ads. Even the pulse comes out with gross errors, and history plus some features sit behind a paywall. Strip away the loud promises and little is left.
apps.loved: The idea of keeping readings in one place
apps.weak: Doesn't measure blood pressure or sugar by camera, misleading ads, pulse errors, history and features locked behind payment, too many ads
apps.whoFor: Essentially no one who expected real measurement, at most as a manual readings diary.

apps.title: Blood Pressure Log, Heart Rate
apps.verdict: The ads make it seem the app measures blood pressure with the phone camera, but really it just logs numbers manually and only reads pulse from the camera. People feel cheated, and full access instantly demands a pricey subscription with no real free option.
apps.loved: Camera pulse reading is fairly accurate, simple data entry
apps.weak: Doesn't measure blood pressure though ads imply it, everything behind a paid subscription, can't try without paying, cluttered entry screen
apps.whoFor: Almost no one, the built in Health app on iPhone does the same for free

quotes.text: there is so much clutter on the BP-entry screen that I can’t navigate from the systolic box down to the diast

apps.title: HeartFit - BP Health Tracker
apps.verdict: It promises to measure pressure and sugar via the camera, but really only measures pulse, and even that is badly off, by 40-50 beats. Pressure and sugar stay unchanged or are not saved, and anything useful is locked behind a weekly subscription. Nurses in the reviews openly doubt that a camera can measure blood pressure.
apps.loved: Handy for tracking pulse, nice to have metrics at hand
apps.weak: Only measures pulse and inaccurately, does not measure pressure or sugar as promised, does not save entered data, expensive subscription, cannot cancel or refund
apps.whoFor: Not for anyone who needs real blood-pressure tracking, there is almost nothing useful behind the paywall

apps.title: Health Care: BP Tracker
apps.verdict: The app advertises camera and finger measurement of blood pressure and sugar, but really only keeps a manual log and buries you in ads. Users flat out say the positive reviews are planted. The camera reads nothing and the promised features are absent.
apps.loved: Almost nothing, the short empty praise looks doubtful
apps.weak: Camera measurement does not work, false ads for sugar and pressure, tons of ads, planted positive reviews, manual entry only
apps.whoFor: No one, the promised camera and finger measurement does not work.

apps.title: InPulse - Heart Rate Monitor
apps.verdict: Promises to measure blood pressure and pulse with the phone camera, but per reviews it doesn't work, readings are random and inflated. It forcibly charges a yearly subscription right after a supposedly free three day trial, and everything free turns out to be paid.
apps.loved: Simple interface, the idea of measuring pulse with the camera
apps.weak: Blood pressure measurement doesn't work, random and inflated readings, deceptive free trial with a yearly charge, impossible to cancel subscription, ads for other apps

apps.title: Health Scan: Heart & Sugar
apps.verdict: The app is sold as a camera-and-finger scanner for blood pressure and sugar, but it is really just a log where you enter readings by hand from real devices. Users complain about misleading free ads, surprise charges and being unable to cancel. The face and finger scans give contradicting numbers and inspire no trust.
apps.loved: Handy for tracking habits, helps keep an eye on health
apps.weak: Does not measure pressure or sugar as advertised, needs external devices, hidden charges, cannot cancel subscription, no refunds, contradictory readings
apps.whoFor: Almost no one: not worth it for camera measurement, and there are more honest manual logs

apps.title: PulsePro:heart&blood monitor
apps.verdict: The app promises to measure blood pressure, sugar and pulse with the camera or a finger, but it really only keeps a manual log. People feel tricked by ads where a finger on the screen supposedly gives readings. A subscription of 8-9 dollars a week for this feels like a rip-off, and cancelling is a struggle.
apps.loved: Simple entry of readings, a tidy diary for those who accept the limits
apps.weak: Deceptive ads about camera measurement, false pulse readings, expensive weekly subscription, hard to cancel, readings not in the right units for Canada
apps.whoFor: People who just want a manual blood pressure journal and expect no phone-based measuring

apps.title: Blood Pressure APP-pulse track
apps.verdict: Sold as a camera measurer of pressure and sugar, but it only measures pulse, while pressure and sugar return the same number day after day. Free is promised, yet real features cost money, and other apps get pushed alongside. Users flatly write that measuring blood pressure with a camera is impossible.
apps.loved: Measures pulse, lets you record data from other sources
apps.weak: Only measures pulse, repeats the same pressure and sugar number, not free despite the promise, pushes other apps, inaccurate readings, confusing interface
apps.whoFor: Not for anyone who needs real blood-pressure tracking, not worth it for camera measurement

apps.title: Blood Pressure Level Checker
apps.verdict: Claims to measure pressure and sugar via the camera through your finger, but numbers diverge wildly from a cuff and often return the exact same result. The 'free' ads mislead, then come forced subscriptions and second charges. The camera frequently just fails to detect the finger.
apps.loved: Simple controls, easy to use at first
apps.weak: Readings far off from a cuff, repeats the same number, lots of ads, a second subscription on top of the first, no support or refunds, camera fails to read the finger
apps.whoFor: Not for anyone who needs real blood-pressure tracking, you will still have to measure with a cuff

quotes.text: it keep sending me a msg all the time to check my blood pressure, even though I just did.

apps.title: iPulse - Check Heart Rate & BP
apps.verdict: The app implies it measures blood pressure and sugar from the phone, but reviews say it only reads pulse and everything else is manual. People get pulled into a yearly subscription with a surprise charge and no clear cancellation. Apple Watch and Health do the same for free.
apps.loved: Almost nothing, the praising five-stars read like ads and inspire no trust
apps.weak: Does not measure pressure or sugar, pulse only, false advertising, hidden subscription charge, no way to cancel, ads every few seconds
apps.whoFor: No one, the promised phone measurement is just pulse, which Apple Watch gives for free.

quotes.text: The app is easy to use and will set three notifications to remind you to take readings daily!

apps.title: Blood Pressure App-Health Body
apps.verdict: Blood Pressure App-Health Body promises automatic measurement, but people say it only shows a canned fake result and nudges you to install more apps. Ads run non-stop, and data still has to be typed in by hand unless you pay. Reviews call the 'completely free' claim an outright lie.
apps.loved: The idea of keeping blood pressure in one place
apps.weak: Doesn't measure pressure, shows a fake result, pushes other apps, flood of ads, manual entry only unless you pay, false 'completely free' claim, hard to cancel
apps.whoFor: No one who expected real measurement, at most as a paid manual diary.

apps.title: Blood Pressure Monitor-BP Log
apps.verdict: Blood Pressure Monitor-BP Log is so buried in ads that even a reading gets interrupted by pop-up banners. It doesn't actually measure pressure, it shows a canned 120 over 80 and pushes you to install another paid app. It's nearly unusable, the ads irritate more than any health benefit.
apps.loved: Almost nothing to highlight
apps.weak: Ads pop up mid-measurement, at least three clips just to take one reading, doesn't measure pressure and shows a fake 120 over 80, pushes another paid app, falsely labeled free
apps.whoFor: No one, a plain notebook is more useful.

apps.title: Blood pressure-i Heart tracker
apps.verdict: The app promises to measure blood pressure, sugar and pulse through the camera, but users comparing it to real devices get wild gaps: the phone shows sugar 80 while the glucometer reads 240. Many call it a subscription scam. It is dangerous to trust these numbers for medication.
apps.loved: Clean interface, promise of tracking everything in one app
apps.weak: Made-up readings, sugar always shows 80, pressure disagrees with a cuff, hidden paid subscription, ads
apps.whoFor: Essentially no one: the numbers cannot be trusted for real blood pressure or sugar control

apps.title: Blood Pressure: Healthy Life
apps.verdict: The app poses as a phone-based blood pressure and sugar meter, but reviews say it measures nothing and repeats identical values. People call it a scam and demand refunds. There is almost no useful function, only heavy advertising.
apps.loved: Almost nothing, the few calm positive reviews are doubtful
apps.weak: Does not measure pressure or sugar, returns identical numbers, misleading ads, heavy advertising, feels like a scam with refund requests
apps.whoFor: Almost no one, the promised phone measurement does not work.

apps.title: Blood Pressure Tracker - Ease
apps.verdict: It claims to measure blood pressure but the app only takes manual entry and drowns the user in ads. Many can't even reach the measurement screen because ads throw them into the App Store. Paying for a subscription doesn't remove the ads, and cancelling turns into a quest.
apps.loved: A few people did build a daily habit of keeping records
apps.weak: A flood of pop-up ads, measurement doesn't work, redirects to the App Store, ads stay even after paying, impossible to find how to cancel
apps.whoFor: Almost nobody, except those willing to endure ads for a plain manual diary

apps.title: QuickPulse: Blood Pressure
apps.verdict: It claims to measure blood pressure but effectively does not: readings either fail to record or freeze on a single value like 110/70. Ads shout about being free, then the second screen demands payment and often denies the trial. A cardiologist in the reviews calls the pulse inaccurate too.
apps.loved: The idea of a quick reading from your phone, portability
apps.weak: Pressure does not measure or repeats the same value, false free promise, payment fails, inaccurate pulse, data-handling concerns
apps.whoFor: Essentially no one: the promised blood pressure measurement is not there

apps.title: HeartSnap:Health Tracker
apps.verdict: The ad promises camera measurement of pressure and sugar, but the app measures nothing and is only a manual log. A finger on the camera gives no result, and money is charged even without a single use, sometimes twice. Users themselves notice the mismatch between the high rating and the flood of one-star complaints.
apps.loved: Information at hand, a handy idea for some
apps.weak: Measures nothing despite the ad, finger on camera does not work, double charges, paid subscription despite promised free, cannot cancel, no refund

apps.title: Heartwell: Track Health
apps.verdict: Ads promise finger sugar readings and pressure, but it actually needs a face scan, and the results are the opposite of the truth: the app scares you about hypertension while the doctor's reading is a normal 124/78. It charges instantly despite the promised free trial. Trusting such health conclusions is dangerous.
apps.loved: The face-scan idea, slick presentation, a few felt it was accurate
apps.weak: False free and sugar-reading ads, results opposite to reality, false hypertension diagnoses, instant charges with no refund
apps.whoFor: No one: the pressure and sugar conclusions are unreliable and can scare you for nothing

apps.title: Health Monitor: Sugar & BP
apps.verdict: The name promises sugar and blood pressure control, but per reviews the app measures neither, only counts pulse and spits out random scary numbers. It disguises a yearly subscription as a free trial, and the rare five stars look like planted filler.
apps.loved: Essentially nothing, maybe the idea of a quick self check for seniors
apps.weak: Measures neither sugar nor pressure despite the name, random scary readings, trial and yearly subscription deception, ads, everything paid to unlock your data

apps.title: Akso: Recording Health
apps.verdict: It is essentially an ad showcase, not an app: any attempt to do something hits banners and redirects to other apps. It does not measure pressure and will not even let you record it properly, history is not saved. Many write that after days they never even saw the app itself because of the ads.
apps.loved: A decent idea in itself
apps.weak: Wall of ads instead of function, constant redirects to other apps, does not measure pressure, does not save history, no promised free tier, impossible to use
apps.whoFor: No one: it is basically unusable because of the ads

apps.title: Health Tracker:Heartrate&BP
apps.verdict: It advertises deviceless sugar and pressure readings via camera or finger, which is physically impossible, and users flatly call it a fraud. Against a cuff the pressure is off by 20-25 points. It charges after a supposedly free trial and is hard to delete.
apps.loved: Almost nothing: a few short, vague praises
apps.weak: Impossible camera measurement of sugar and pressure, false free advertising, hidden charges, the app reinstalls itself, ads on every tap
apps.whoFor: No one: this is a dangerous imitation of medical measurement

apps.title: BloodPressure-Level Checker
apps.verdict: Users cannot even reach a measurement because of wall-to-wall ads that pop up after every action and push installs of other apps. When a reading does happen, pressure runs 15-19 points below the doctor's. It is essentially an ad dump disguised as a health app.
apps.loved: Almost nothing: a few short praises, often contradicting the stars given
apps.weak: Relentless intrusive ads, impossible to reach a measurement, understated pressure, pushes other app installs, still broken after paying
apps.whoFor: No one: the measurement is unreachable behind ads and the numbers cannot be trusted

quotes.text: it keep sending me a msg all the time to check my blood pressure, even though I just did.

apps.title: Blood Pressure：Scan Health
apps.verdict: By the reviews this is an ad shell where the actual function is lost behind a dozen pop-ups. There is no blood pressure or sugar measurement and the finger on the camera does nothing. People call it a scam and spam, and some fear a virus.
apps.loved: Almost nothing, the single five-star about removing ads for a fee is doubtful
apps.weak: Wall-to-wall pop-up ads, does not measure pressure or sugar, finger on camera does nothing, App Store redirects, feels like a scam and spam
apps.whoFor: No one, it is essentially an ad redirect with no working function.
